rule_in_words: For births up to the early 1970s most states let a child start kindergarten (or first grade where kindergarten was not universal) in September if they turned 5 (or 6) by 31 December or a date between 1 September and 1 February; in 1975 only 9 of the 30 states with a statutory cutoff used September or earlier and 20 states left the date to districts.
notes: ECS 2007 'Kindergarten Entrance Ages: A 30 Year Trend Analysis' (archived copy). Deming and Dynarski 2008 (NBER w14124, JEP 22(3)) describe the typical early-20th-century rule as turning six by the end of December to start first grade in September. Angrist and Krueger 1991 used the same rule. Use the state rows for a founder's birth state where known.

rule_in_words: Transition period: states moved their cutoffs earlier one by one, so cohorts born 1971 to 1985 faced a mix of 31 December-type and 1 September-type rules; the share of states with a September-or-earlier cutoff rose from 30% (1975) to 67% (1990).
notes: Deming and Dynarski 2008 fig. 3: the average statutory date by which a child must be five moved from about 31 December toward 1 September between 1965 and 2005. See the state rows for the 1975/1990/2005 snapshots.

notes: NCES Table 5.3 (2018) reproduces the ECS 50-State Comparison; ECS 2011 update: 36 of 45 states with a date used September or earlier in 2010 (80%). rule_in_words: Before the 1986 Compulsory Education Law there was no national statutory cutoff; children started primary school at 6 or 7 depending on province and on urban or rural location.
notes: Not sourced for the pre-1986 era: write 'unknown'. The 1986 law (art. 5) allows areas that cannot manage age 6 to start at 7.

rule_in_words: A child who has turned 6 by 31 August starts primary school on 1 September; the 1986 Compulsory Education Law sets age 6 (7 where local conditions do not permit) and since 2017 provinces may set the exact date, but 31 August remains the common rule nationwide.
notes: Law text: lexiscn.com translation of the Compulsory Education Law (art. 5 of 1986 text = art. 11 of 2006 revision). Relative-age studies using the 31 August cutoff: Zhang and Xie (Princeton), Liu and Li 2015.

rule_in_words: No single national rule; most states and the Kendriya Vidyalaya system admitted a child to Class 1 if aged 5 by 31 March (the academic year starts in April), while Karnataka used 1 June and some states 30 September.
notes: Varies by state and school board; KVS pre-2022 guideline: '5 years old as on 31st March'. A December 2023 Rajya Sabha reply said 13 states/UTs still admitted at 5+ and 21 at 6+.

rule_in_words: Under NEP 2020 the Ministry of Education asked all states to admit to Class 1 only children aged 6+; KVS and CBSE schools use 31 March as the reference date (a child born on 1 April is also admitted); states adopted the change between 2022 and 2026, some with phased relaxations.
notes: KVS revised guidelines 2022-23: minimum 6, maximum 8 as on 31 March. Goa uses 1 June as reference date.

rule_in_words: A child enters elementary school in the first school year (starting 1 April) that begins after the day following their 6th birthday, so a cohort runs from 2 April to 1 April and children born on 1 April are the youngest.
notes: School Education Act (Act No. 26 of 1947) art. 17(1); TIMSS 2019: 'Children must be 6 years old by April 1'. The April cohort predates 1947 (pre-war school ordinances), not verified here. Relative-age evidence: Kawaguchi (ESRI/Hitotsubashi).

rule_in_words: A child who had turned 6 by the end of February entered elementary school on 1 March; a cohort ran from 1 March to the end of February (the 2007 intake was children born 1 March 2000 to end of February 2001).
notes: Hangyo (Yonhap) 14 Sep 2006, announcing the amendment of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act. Leap-year births on 29 February belong to this cohort.

rule_in_words: Since the 2009 intake the reference date is 1 January: a child who turns 6 by 31 December enters the following March, so cohorts are calendar years; the 2009 intake was a transition cohort (born March to December 2002) and from 2010 cohorts are full calendar years.
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'Children must be 6 years old by December 31 to begin school the following March'. Transition detail from Hangyo 2008 reporting (no=17371). Parents may choose entry one year early or late. Kim (2021, J. Demographic Economics) and Cho and Lee (2020) document birth-timing and registration responses to the change.

rule_in_words: A child who has turned 6 on or before 1 September starts elementary school that September; children born on 2 September or later wait a year.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 (Chinese Taipei); Taipei City administrative decision citing the National Education Act enforcement rules (laws.gov.taipei/law/LawDecision/ContentExport?id=791-057). Rule confirmed for 2006 and 2019 intakes; start year of the rule not sourced (nine-year compulsory education dates from 1968).

rule_in_words: A child aged 5 years 8 months by 1 September (born on or before 31 December of the previous year) is eligible for Primary One, so the cohort is the calendar year of birth.
notes: EDB Primary One Admission: the 2026 intake covers children born on or before 31 December 2020. TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. Era not sourced; the central POA system dates from 1983.

rule_in_words: A child who has turned 6 by 1 January (the day before the school year starts) enters Primary 1 that January; eligible birthdays run from 2 January of one year to 1 January of the next (born 2 Jan 2020 to 1 Jan 2021 for the 2027 intake).
notes: TIMSS 2019 confirms the 2 January to 1 January cohort; parents of 1 January children may defer a year. Compulsory Education Act in force since 2003; the cohort rule predates it (era not sourced).

rule_in_words: Education Act 1996 s.29A: a child who has attained 6 on 1 January of the school year must be enrolled in primary school that year, so the cohort is in effect the calendar year of birth and children start Year 1 at 6 turning 7.
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'Children who are 6 years old by January 1 begin school in January of that academic year'. Malay Mail 23 Jan 2026 quotes s.29A(2); optional entry at 6 announced for 2027. Pre-1996 rule not sourced.

rule_in_words: A child must be at least 6 on 1 July of the enrolment year to enter grade 1 of primary school (SD); 7-year-olds have priority and children of 5 years 6 months may be admitted with a psychologist's or teachers' recommendation.
notes: Permendikbud 14/2018 and 1/2021 (PPDB rules); earlier regulations stated the same 6/7 rule. Pre-2010s practice not sourced.

rule_in_words: Compulsory Education Act B.E. 2545 (2002): a child must enter grade 1 in the school year (starting in May) of the calendar year in which they are 'entering the seventh year of age', i.e. the year they turn 6; age is counted by calendar year of birth under a ministerial regulation.
notes: Only the Act's phrase and the existence of the age-counting regulation were sourced; the regulation text itself was not read. Pre-2002 (Primary Education Act 1980, compulsory from 'entering the eighth year') not sourced: unknown.

rule_in_words: Grade 1 entry is at age 6 counted by calendar year: children born in a given year start in September of the year they turn 6 (Education Law 2019 art. 28; the 1998 and 2005 laws set the same age).
notes: Circular 28/2020/TT-BGDDT: age calculated in years; medRxiv 2024 study describes the cutoff as turning 6 by 31 December. Era start not sourced.

rule_in_words: A child who was 6 by the opening of classes in early June could enrol in Grade 1 (DepEd order of 2006); kindergarten became compulsory in 2012.
notes: The opening date of classes varied (first or second week of June), so no fixed month-day. Pre-2006 practice not sourced.

rule_in_words: DepEd Order 16 s.2015: Grade 1 entrants must be at least 6 by 31 October of the school year.
notes: Kindergarten entrants had to be 5 by 1 June from 2016-17 under the same order (reported by DepEd); the Grade 1 and Kindergarten dates therefore differed.

rule_in_words: DepEd Order 3 s.2018 (Basic Education Enrollment Policy): Kindergarten at 5 by 31 August, Grade 1 at 6 by 31 August of the school year.
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'at least 6 years old by August 31 of the school year they will enroll'. Manila Bulletin 29 Jan 2019 reports the same.

rule_in_words: TIMSS 2019 national coordinator: a child must be 6 by 31 March to begin school the following April; in practice provinces and private schools admit at 5 with their own reference dates, so there is no uniform national rule.
notes: Rawalpindi (2026) sets Grade 1 minimum at 5; Islamabad FDE uses maximum ages with a 3-month relaxation. Treat as unknown for most cohorts.

rule_in_words: A child must have turned 6 by 21/22 September (31 Shahrivar, the day before the school year opens on 1 Mehr) to enter grade 1; children born in Mehr have at times been admitted by exception.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021: 'Children must be 6 years old by September 21'. The Persian-calendar date falls on 21 or 22 September in the Gregorian calendar. Era not sourced.

rule_in_words: Children start grade 1 in the September of the year in which they turn 6; the cutoff is set by the Hebrew calendar (reported as 1 Tevet, which falls in December or early January), so the Gregorian date shifts each year; TIMSS and PIRLS describe it as the calendar year of the 6th birthday.
notes: Hebrew-calendar cutoff per Nefesh B'Nefesh guide (nbn.org.il); one report gives 9 Tevet under a 1959 law. Official Ministry page not reachable. For most founders the calendar year (12-31) is a close approximation.

rule_in_words: A child who completed 72 months (age 6) by 31 December of the enrolment year started grade 1 in September, so the cohort was the calendar year and children were 5 years 8 months to 6 years 8 months at entry.
notes: MEB official quoted on the previous regulation: '31 Aralik itibariyla 72 ayini dolduran'. Hurriyet/bianet describe children starting at 6.5 to 7 before 2012.

rule_in_words: 4+4+4 reform (Law 6287, regulation of 21 July 2012): children who completed 66 months by the end of September were enrolled in grade 1; 60 to 65-month-olds could enrol on written parental request.
notes: First-grade classes in 2012-13 mixed children aged 60 to 84 months.

rule_in_words: Children who complete 69 months by the end of September must enrol (66 to 68 months on parental request; those who will reach 69 months by 31 December may also be enrolled on request); TIMSS 2019 records the June 2019 reaffirmation of 69 months.
notes: Sources differ on whether a 31 December reference also applies; the 2014 and 2019 regulations use end of September.

rule_in_words: A child must have turned 6 by the first day of the school year, with a tolerance of up to 90 days (for 1448 AH: born on or before 24 August 2020, with the 90-day grace reaching about 23 November); the Gregorian date moves with the academic calendar.
notes: TIMSS 2019: '6 years old by 90 days after the first day of school'; PIRLS 2021: by the first day of the school year. Okaz (okaz.com.sa/local/na/2239326) gives the 2020 dates. Era not sourced.

rule_in_words: Before 2013 children could start grade 1 at 5 years 6 months; the reference date was not sourced.
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'Before 2013, children could begin school at age 5.5'.

rule_in_words: From 2013 a child had to be 6 by 31 December of the year of enrolment to enter grade 1.
Ministerial Resolution 24/2021: a child must be 6 (and not more than 8) by 31 August of the admission year for schools starting in September (31 March for schools starting in April).
notes: PIRLS 2021 confirms.

rule_in_words: For admissions from 2026-27 the cutoff moves back to 31 December of the admission year (new admissions only; April-start schools keep 31 March).

Year groups run from 1 September to 31 August; children start reception in the September after their 4th birthday and schooling is compulsory from the term after the 5th birthday (prescribed days 31 December, 31 March, 31 August); until about 2011 many authorities admitted children termly, which does not change the year-group cohort.
notes: House of Commons Library briefing 7272 'Summer-born children: starting school'; PIRLS 2021 England entry; NI Assembly briefing NIAR 118-2021 for Wales. 'Summer born' = 1 April to 31 August.

rule_in_words: School starts in August and a year group is children born from 1 March of one year to the end of February of the next, so pupils are 4.5 to 5.5 at entry; children born January to February (and since August 2023 all those still 4 in August) may defer a year with funded nursery.
notes: Also Angus Council guidance (angus.gov.uk/node/3187) and Fife Council. Long-standing rule (Education (Scotland) Act 1980 s.32), start year not sourced; 29 February births belong to the cohort.

rule_in_words: A child who has turned 4 on or before 1 July starts P1 the following September (Education Reform (NI) Order 1989; Article 46 of the Education and Libraries (NI) Order 1986), so the cohort is born 2 July to 1 July and the youngest start at 4 years 2 months.
notes: Deferral legislation for the youngest was announced in 2021 (School Age Act (NI) 2022, not verified here). TIMSS 2019 confirms.

rule_in_words: Before 1990 compulsory schooling began at 5 as in England (term after the fifth birthday); the year-group boundary used before the 1989 Order was not sourced.

No statutory cutoff: children may start primary school (junior infants) from age 4 and must be in school by 6; each school sets its own enrolment age rule, and the share starting at 5 rose from 52% (2000) to 72% (2017).
notes: Oireachtas written answer 27 Sep 2022 (oireachtas.ie/en/debates/question/2022-09-27/227/); Irish Times 2017/2018. Bedard and Dhuey excluded Ireland for this reason.

rule_in_words: Nationwide 'for a long time' a child who had turned 6 by 30 June started school on 1 August of that year (the KMK Hamburg Agreement of 1964 set this date; not verified here).
notes: Bildungsserver: 'Lange Zeit galt der 30. Juni als der allgemeine Stichtag'. The 1964 origin is standard in the literature (e.g. Puhani and Weber 2007) but was not read directly.

rule_in_words: Since the 1997 KMK decision each Land sets a date between 30 June and 30 September; 30 September (NRW, Bayern with a 1 July to 30 September deferral option, Niedersachsen, Berlin) covers most of the population, while nine Länder use 30 June or 1 July, Rheinland-Pfalz 31 August and Thüringen 1 August.
notes: By count of Länder 30 June is the most common date; by population 30 September. Use the Land rows where the founder's Land is known. Bildungsserver table (Stichtage 2027) and TIMSS 2019/PIRLS 2021 Germany entries.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts school that September; 30 September applied from 2007/08 until 2019/20.
notes: Landtag press release 69/2019: committee votes to move the Stichtag from 30 September back to 30 June from 2020/21; it notes the 30 September shift was introduced in 2007/08.

rule_in_words: Children who turn 6 by 30 June must start; children turning 6 from 1 July to 30 September also become schulpflichtig unless their parents postpone to the next year (Einschulungskorridor), so the effective cutoff is 30 September with a parental opt-out.
notes: Art. 37(1) BayEUG. Years of the earlier moves (30 June to 30 September in the 2000s; Korridor from 2019/20) not verified here.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 September starts on 1 August; 31 December applied from the 2005 primary-school reform until 2016, and 30 June before 2005.
notes: Early entry on application for children turning 6 between 1 October and 31 March (Bildungsserver).

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts school; 30 September applied before the change announced in 2020 for the 2022 intake.
notes: de.wikipedia cites rbb24 (Sept 2020) on the move; the Bildungsserver 2027 table still shows 30 September with admission on application for 1 October to 31 December births, so verify before use.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts school; children turning 6 from 1 July to 30 September may choose this year or next.
Children born from 2 July of one year to 1 July of the next become schulpflichtig on 1 August (e.g. born 2 July 2020 to 1 July 2021 for 2027/28); later births may enter early on application.
A child who turns 6 by 30 June (sources also phrase it as 'born up to and including 1 July') starts on 1 August; later births are Kann-Kinder who may enter on application.
notes: Hessisches Schulgesetz § 58.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts on 1 August; children turning 6 by 30 June of the following year may be admitted on application.
A child who turns 6 by 30 September becomes schulpflichtig; parents of children born 1 July to 30 September may defer a year (Flexibilisierung).
notes: Kultusministerium information page on the flexibilised Stichtag (mk.niedersachsen.de) not reachable; year of the move from 30 June not verified.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 September becomes schulpflichtig on 1 August of the same year; children turning 6 from 1 October start the following year, early entry on request.
notes: § 35 SchulG NRW. PIRLS 2021 notes NRW changed its cut-off dates in the 2010s; the step-wise move from 30 June (2007-2009) not verified here.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 before 1 September (i.e. by 31 August) becomes schulpflichtig; younger children may be admitted on application.
notes: Bildungsserver agrees (31 August).

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts at the beginning of the school year; children turning 6 later in the calendar year or the next may be admitted early on application.
notes: Saarland Schulpflichtgesetz § 1 (recht.saarland.de) not reachable.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts school; Kann-Kinder on parental request.
A child who turns 6 by 30 June starts school; children who have turned 5 by 30 June may enrol if ready.
A child who turns 6 by 30 June of the current year starts school; later births may enter early on application.
A child who has turned 6 by 1 August becomes schulpflichtig; children at least 5 on 30 June may be registered.
notes: Bildungsserver table agrees (1 August); de.wikipedia Schulpflicht gives 31 July.

rule_in_words: Children enter CP (first year of elementary school) in September of the calendar year in which they turn 6, with no maturity test; since 2019 instruction is compulsory from age 3 on the same calendar-year basis.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. Compulsory from 6 since the Ferry law of 1882 (not verified here); era start left blank.

rule_in_words: Under the pre-1985 kleuterschool/lagere school system a child had to be 6 by 1 October to enter the first class of primary school (lagere school) in August.
notes: Rijksoverheid: the 1 October rule has not existed since August 1985 but some schools still apply it. Era start not sourced.

rule_in_words: Since the 1985 Primary Education Act children start basisschool the day after their 4th birthday (compulsory from 5) and the school decides when a child moves to groep 3, the first formal grade; many schools still use 1 October or 1 January as the dividing line ('najaarskinderen').
notes: CPB seminar summary: 'For a long period Dutch schools used being born before October 1 as cut-off rule'. Bedard and Dhuey excluded the Netherlands for this reason. TIMSS 2019: kindergarten compulsory from the month after the 5th birthday.

rule_in_words: A child is admitted to primary school on 1 September of the calendar year in which they turn 6 (compulsory from that date under the law of 29 June 1983; since 1 September 2020 compulsory from 5, also by calendar year).
notes: TIMSS 2019 (Flemish) and PIRLS 2021 (French and Flemish) confirm the calendar-year cohort. Compulsory from 6 also before 1983 (law of 1914), not verified here.

rule_in_words: Before the HarmoS concordat each canton set its own cutoff, mostly between early April and late July (Zürich and Basel-Stadt 30 April, St. Gallen 1 August); children entered kindergarten at 4 to 5 and grade 1 two years later.
notes: Zürich cantonal parliament documents (parlzhcdws.cmicloud.ch) record the move from 30 April to 31 July. Bedard and Dhuey excluded Switzerland for this reason.

rule_in_words: HarmoS art. 5: a child who has turned 4 by 31 July enters kindergarten in August and grade 1 two years later (turned 6 by 31 July); adopted by 15 cantons and phased in between 2009 and about 2019 (Basel-Landschaft 2012/13 to 2017/18, Zürich complete by 2019); non-member cantons keep their own dates.
notes: Solothurn government answer 2024 (so.ch) on the 15 member cantons; Basel-Landschaft press release on the staged move. A 2025 Zürich motion seeks a return to 30 April.

rule_in_words: Compulsory schooling begins on the 1 September following a child's 6th birthday, so children who turn 6 on or before 31 August start that September (Schulpflichtgesetz 1985 § 2; for premature babies the due date may be used).
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. The 1985 act consolidated the 1962 Schulpflichtgesetz with the same rule (not verified here). Early admission possible for children turning 6 by 1 March of the following year.

rule_in_words: Children start grade 1 in the autumn of the calendar year they turn 7 (preschool class in the year they turn 6, compulsory since 2018); on request a child may start at 6 or 8.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. Government plans to start school at 6 from 2028. Era start not sourced (long-standing).

rule_in_words: Before the kindergarten class became compulsory, compulsory schooling (grade 1) began in the calendar year a child turned 7; most children attended the optional kindergarten class at 6.
notes: PIRLS 2016: 'One year of preprimary school is now compulsory' (change within the previous ten years); the August 2009 start of compulsory kindergarten class is from the Folkeskole Act amendment of 2008 (not read directly).

rule_in_words: Ten years of compulsory schooling (kindergarten class, grade 0, through grade 9) begin in August of the calendar year a child turns 6; early entry for children turning 5 before 1 October and one-year deferral on request.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm the calendar-year cohort.

rule_in_words: Children started grade 1 in the calendar year they turned 7.
notes: 'Before 1997, mandatory education in Norway started at the age of 7.' Calendar-year reckoning for the pre-1997 era inferred from the current rule; not separately sourced.

rule_in_words: Since Reform 97 children start grade 1 in August of the calendar year they turn 6; early entry for children turning 5 between 1 January and 31 March, or deferral, on recommendation.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021: 'Children begin school during the calendar year of their sixth birthday'.

rule_in_words: Children start basic education in August of the calendar year they turn 7 (Basic Education Act 628/1998 § 25); parents may request a start one year earlier or later.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. The same rule applied under earlier acts (not verified here).

rule_in_words: Children are enrolled in primary education in the calendar year in which they turn 6 (LOE 2006 as amended by LOMLOE 2020), so the cohort is the calendar year.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. Same calendar-year rule under LOGSE 1990 and the 1970 General Education Act (not verified here).

rule_in_words: Children who turn 6 by 31 December of the year the school year starts must enrol in the first year of primary school; children turning 6 by 30 April of the following year may enrol early (anticipatari).
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 confirm. Early entry introduced by D.Lgs. 59/2004 (not verified here).

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 15 September must enrol in the 1st cycle of basic education that September; children turning 6 between 16 September and 31 December may be enrolled conditionally at the parents' request.
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'turn 6 years old by the beginning of the school year (mid-September)'; PIRLS 2016 and 2021 agree; Lei de Bases 1986 art. 6 uses 15 September (not read directly).

rule_in_words: Children started grade 1 in September of the calendar year they turned 7.
Phased reform: in September 2014 children born January to June 2008 had to start at 6; in September 2015 all children turning 6 in the calendar year started.
notes: Eurydice 'Compulsory Education in Europe 2014/15' describes the half-cohort rule; TIMSS 2019 dates the lowering to 2015.

rule_in_words: From September 2016 the entry age reverted to 7 (calendar year) with an option to start at 6 after a preparatory year.
A child who turned 6 by 31 May started school in September of that calendar year; deferral to 7 or 8 was common.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2016 (change in January 2013). Era start not sourced (1993 Public Education Act used the same date).

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 31 August becomes tanköteles and starts in September (Act CXC of 2011, applied from 2013); since 2020 deferral needs the education authority's approval.

A child who turns 6 by 31 August starts in September; children born September to December may start early with a readiness assessment, and roughly a fifth of children defer a year (Education Act 561/2004 § 36).
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'birthdays before September 1 begin at the start of the academic year'. The same rule applied in Czechoslovakia (not verified here).

rule_in_words: A pupil must have turned 6 by 31 December of the enrolment year to enter the first grade of primary school in September, so the cohort is the calendar year.
notes: Era start not sourced (Law 1566/1985 and earlier).

rule_in_words: All children aged 4 before 1 September must attend fundamental school (cycle 1); cycle 2 (the first primary grade) follows two years later for children aged 6 before 1 September, so cohorts run 1 September to 31 August.
notes: Loi du 6 février 2009 relative à l'obligation scolaire. Before 2009 primary was compulsory from 6 before 1 September with compulsory preschool from 5 (1963) and 4 (1992), not verified here.

rule_in_words: Soviet children entered grade 1 at 7 (the entry age was lowered from 8 to 7 during the Second World War); the exact birthday rule used to form cohorts was not sourced; the 1984 reform planned entry at 6.
notes: Also applies to Soviet-era Ukraine. Write 'unknown' rather than assume 1 September.

rule_in_words: A child must be at least 6 years 6 months on 1 September (born on or before 1 March) and not older than 8; the school founder may admit younger or older children on request, and most children start at about 7 (Federal Law 273-FZ art. 67; the 1992 Law on Education set the same minimum).
notes: TIMSS 2019: 'Children must be 6.5 years old by September 1'; PIRLS 2021 phrases it as 6 by 1 March. The 1992 start year for the 6.5 rule was not verified here.

rule_in_words: Soviet-era rule as for Russia: entry at 7, birthday rule not sourced.

Primary education normally begins at 6: a child who has turned 6 by the start of the school year (1 September) enters grade 1, parents may delay a year, and children who are 7 at the start of the school year must begin that year (Law on Education 2145-VIII art. 12).
notes: Law text not fetched directly (site unreachable); wording confirmed from school admission documents quoting art. 12. Entry at 6 also under the 1999 Law on General Secondary Education (not verified).

rule_in_words: In every province and territory except Quebec a child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September and grade 1 the next year, so cohorts are calendar years; Quebec uses 30 September.
notes: OISE 'Kindergarten and Pre-Kindergarten in Canada' chart, updated 11 April 2025; Alberta school-district notice: all provinces except Quebec use 31 December. Historical exceptions: Alberta boards (1 March) until 2020, Saskatoon (31 January) until 2025, PEI (31 October) until the early 2010s. Bedard and Dhuey 2006 used provincial cutoffs for NLSCY.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September.

A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September (children born September to December may enrol the following year); the cutoff was moved from 31 October to 31 December in phases in the early 2010s.
notes: PEI government release on the age-of-entry policy (archivenews.princeedwardisland.ca) describes the 31 October to 31 December change; exact year not sourced.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters Grade Primary in September; September to December births may wait a year.
A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September; September to December births may wait a year.
A child who turns 5 by 30 September enters kindergarten (maternelle) and one who turns 6 before 1 October enters grade 1 in late August (Loi sur l'instruction publique).
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 Quebec entries confirm 'before October 1'.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 4 by 31 December enters junior kindergarten and 5 by 31 December senior kindergarten in September; compulsory from 6 (Education Act s.33).
notes: TIMSS 2019 Ontario entry: children with sixth birthdays before 31 December may begin grade 1 in September.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September.
School divisions set the date; all but Saskatoon used 31 December, and Saskatoon Public and Greater Saskatoon Catholic moved from 31 January to 31 December for fall 2025.
notes: OISE: 'School divisions establish age of entry'.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September (province-wide since 1 September 2020); before that each board chose, with Edmonton Public and Edmonton Catholic requiring 5 by 1 March and others 31 December.
notes: Global News 2016 and CTV Edmonton on the Education Act amendment.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten in September (School Act s.3).
A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten.
A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten.
A child who turns 5 by 31 December enters kindergarten.
A child had to have turned 6 before 1 September to enter first grade of primary school that school year.
notes: Peña (2017, Economics of Education Review 56) and a Columbia dissertation: 'prior to the 2006-2007 school year, the cut-off day for school entry in Mexico had been September 1st'; SEP 2005 announcement (El Siglo de Torreón) says the same.

rule_in_words: From the 2006-07 school year a child who turns 6 by 31 December of the year of entry may start first grade in August (SEP norm adopted by most states that year, Tlaxcala among the first; Aguayo-Téllez and Martínez-Rodríguez 2020 report that many states later moved to 31 August, but 2026 SEP preinscripción notices for CDMX and Nuevo León still use 31 December).
notes: Peña 2017 studies the four-month shift; Aguayo-Téllez and Martínez-Rodríguez 2020 (Large-scale Assessments in Education) use PISA 2018 on the 2006 cohort.

rule_in_words: Under the 1996 LDB children entered the eight-year ensino fundamental at 7, and each state set its own reference date (São Paulo used 30 June).
notes: Earlier cohorts (1930s to 1990s) also entered at 7 under state rules; exact dates not sourced.

rule_in_words: Law 11.274/2006 made entry at 6 compulsory with a nine-year ensino fundamental; states had until 2010 to implement and kept their own cutoffs meanwhile.
CNE/CEB resolutions 1/2010 and 6/2010 (reaffirmed by resolution 2/2018) require a child to have turned 6 by 31 March of the enrolment year to enter the first year of ensino fundamental.
notes: PIRLS 2021 Brazil entry (LDB art. 32); the date was challenged in ADI 17 and ADPF 292 (decided 2018).

rule_in_words: A child who turns 6 by 30 June of the school year enters first grade in March (Buenos Aires Province Decree 538/82; the national Ley 26.206 and Federal Council resolutions use the same 30 June reference).
notes: Decree of 17 June 1982: 'Podrán ser inscriptos en el primer grado los niños que cumplan 6 años al 30 de Junio'. Federal Council resolution not fetched; UNLP 2022 regulation uses 'antes del 1 de julio'.

rule_in_words: A child who has turned 6 by 31 March of the year of entry enters 1° básico in March (Decreto Exento 1126/2017); the earlier Decreto 1718/2011 let school directors extend the date to 30 June.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2016 confirm 31 March with principal discretion to 30 June/1 July. Pre-2011 rules not sourced; LOCE 1990 set age 6 without a date.

rule_in_words: Rules differ by state; the first (pre-Year 1) year starts in late January and a child must have turned 5 by a state date between 1 January (Tasmania) and 31 July (NSW); 30 June (Queensland, Western Australia, Northern Territory) is the most common date by count, 31 July (NSW) covers the largest population.
notes: Scouts Australia 'School Age Summary Report' (Dec 2014) table; The Conversation 28 Aug 2023; TIMSS 2019 Australia entry. Bedard and Dhuey excluded Australia for this reason. Use the state rows.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 on or before 31 July starts Kindergarten that year and must be enrolled by their 6th birthday.
notes: Scouts 2014 table agrees. Start year of the 31 July rule not sourced.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 30 April starts Foundation (Prep) that year; school is compulsory from 6.

A child who turns 5 by 30 June starts Prep that year and must be enrolled in the year they turn 6 by 30 June; 2007 (first full Prep year) used 5 years 6 months by 31 December; from 1987 to 2006 Year 1 entry required turning 5 by 31 December of the previous year, and 1971 to 1985 turning 5 by the last day of February.
notes: Queensland Government history page 'School admission and progression age' (1875-2008). A 31 July option in 2014 was reversed in 2015.

rule_in_words: Since 2014 a child who turns 5 before 1 May starts Reception at the beginning of the year (a mid-year intake was added in 2023); before 2014 children started Reception in the term after their 5th birthday.
notes: TIMSS 2019 Australia entry; Scouts 2014 table gives 'on or before 1 May' (the state rule is 'before 1 May', i.e. 30 April inclusive).

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 by 30 June starts Pre-primary (compulsory since 2013; introduced 2002) that year.
notes: TIMSS 2019: Pre-primary introduced 2002, compulsory 2013. Pre-2002 Year 1 rule not sourced.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 on or before 1 January starts Prep that year (Kindergarten at 4 by 1 January); compulsory from 5.
notes: Scouts 2014 table; the 2016 Education Act briefly allowed starting at 4.5. Official DECYP page not reachable.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 on or before 30 April starts Kindergarten that year.
notes: Scouts 2014 table agrees.

rule_in_words: A child who turns 5 on or before 30 June starts Transition that year; the NT moved to a single start-of-year entry in the 2010s.
notes: Scouts 2014 table agrees; TIMSS 2019 notes the move to a single point of entry.

rule_in_words: No fixed cohort cutoff: children may start on their 5th birthday (any school day) and must be enrolled by 6; each school decides Year 0/Year 1 placement (often by whether the child started before mid-year), and since 2020 schools may adopt cohort entry at the start or middle of each term.
notes: TIMSS 2019 and PIRLS 2021 New Zealand entries. Relative age in NZ depends on school-level year-group rules; Bedard and Dhuey 2006 used NZ data with a birthday-entry assumption.

rule_in_words: Admission ages before the 1998 national policy were set by the separate education departments of the apartheid era and were not sourced.
Government Notice 2433 of 1998 (Admission Policy for Ordinary Public Schools) set the Grade 1 admission age at 7 turning in the calendar year (statistical age norm = grade + 6).
notes: Amended by GN 1356 of 2001 after Harris v Minister of Education (not read).

rule_in_words: A child may enter Grade 1 if aged 5 turning 6 by 30 June of the admission year (SASA s.5(4) as amended in 2002); the statistical norm remains 6 turning 7, and TIMSS/PIRLS describe the cohort as the calendar year of the 7th birthday.
notes: Western Cape circular agrees. The 2004 start year for the amended rule was not verified here. Many children still enter at 6 turning 7, so the effective cohort straddles two rules.

rule_in_words: The National Policy on Education sets Primary 1 entry at age 6, but no national birthday cutoff was found; states and schools apply their own.
notes: News reports quoting NPE 2013 s.2(17). Write 'unknown'.

rule_in_words: A child must be 6 by 1 October (the start of the school year) to enter grade 1 (Education Law 139/1981 art. 15: age 6, admission from 5 and a half where places exist).
notes: TIMSS 2019: '6 years old by the beginning of October'; PIRLS 2016/2021: by the end of September. Law text at manshurat.org/node/63716. Pre-1981 (Law 68/1968) not sourced.
